title: Recovered wages can remain practically unreachable when worker location, identity, claim effort, and payment access are unresolved
source_unit: U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division Workers Owed Wages public recovery route
geography: United States; DOL Wage and Hour Division

observations.period: Current Workers Owed Wages route checked September 19, 2026

denominator.unit: workers for whom WHD recovered unpaid wages; no public episode denominator or same-worker outcome panel

institutional_recovery.value: WHD may recover unpaid wages and hold them while attempting to locate and notify the worker

claim_requirements.value: worker searches the system, verifies identity, supplies contact information, signs a claim form, uploads documents, and uses the payment route

holding_period.unit: years wages are held while WHD attempts to locate an employee before remaining funds go to Treasury

worker_receipt.unit: missing location, notice receipt, claim effort, payment date, cashing, fees, adequacy, household effect, later work, trust, recurrence, and exit

mechanism.value: Institutional recovery can be complete in agency custody while remaining practically unusable to a worker who cannot be located, notified, verified, or reached through payment

observations.method: Structured extraction from official DOL Workers Owed Wages page and claim instructions; agency recovery, search/notice, worker claim requirements, holding period, and missing recipient outcomes are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The public route does not identify worker, amount, address history, notice delivery, claim effort, identity documents, payment date, cashing, fees, adequacy, household effect, later work, trust, recurrence, or exit.
observations.subgroup: Workers for whom WHD recovered unpaid wages; no public worker-level, employer-level, wage-loss, demographic, or payment outcome subgroup is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A searchable route and three-year holding period can preserve a meaningful claim opportunity, but they do not show that a worker knew about, could complete, or could use the route.

observations.period: Electronic-payment transition beginning October 1, 2025; instructions checked September 19, 2026

denominator.unit: workers receiving or expecting back wages through WOW; recipient-level transition denominator not disclosed

payment_channel.value: electronic payments replaced the prior paper-check route for the described transition

digital_identity_requirements.value: contact information, signed claim form, login.gov access, and identity documentation are required before processing

processing_expectation.value: approximately six weeks after claim submission

payment_completion.unit: missing update completion, claim acceptance, electronic delivery, cashing, fees, adequacy, household relief, and later work

mechanism.value: Electronic delivery may standardize payment for workers with stable digital access while transferring contact, documentation, login, and account-readiness risk to recipients

observations.method: Structured extraction from current official DOL Workers Owed Wages payment instructions; channel transition and recipient requirements are retained separately from successful completion and receipt.
observations.uncertainty: The guidance does not provide a recipient-level transition denominator, paper-check failure rate, update effort, claim submission, payment date, delivery, cashing, fee, adequacy, household effect, or later work outcome.
observations.subgroup: Workers moving from paper-check to electronic WOW payment instructions; no subgroup outcome by digital access, identity documentation, geography, age, or disability is published.
observations.counterinterpretation: Electronic payment can be easier for one worker and a barrier for another; the route description cannot identify which experience occurred.

boundary: This record establishes an institutional wage-recovery and reachability architecture. It does not establish worker-level payment, adequacy, household recovery, trust, durable security, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from official DOL Workers Owed Wages pages; worker, wage, claim, identity, bank, and restricted data are not retained.
